claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, is current implementation truth and says the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md, recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00, is historical evidence: its passing retrieval test corpus, healthy `/ready` result, and proposal to open owner alpha immediately predate the production-sized findings and must not override the newer note.

Although connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval against the owner corpus—about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens—are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, failure of a later lane can also discard an earlier lane’s successful result.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. With about 64,000 active records already present, this creates write amplification tied to total corpus membership rather than merely the changed files and contributes to the conclusion that the architecture is not dependable at 10x corpus growth.

The approved direction—still a proposal rather than verified completed implementation—is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets.
